column1: # vdi-raster-screen32.tsv -- NewTOS contract (ADR-038), 32-plane setting: no oracle.
# The 32-plane twin of vdi-raster-screen.tsv (TASK/V69): the VDI raster
# group with the SCREEN as an operand, at vdiplanes=32. A WIDE table
# (tosdump/core/cases.h, "THE 32-PLANE SETTING"): it declares a 32-plane
# screen, so DUMPRAST runs it only at 32 planes, writes the wide record
# (area 7 VDI-RASTER32, 5744 bytes, buffers of 1024 WORDs, the readback
# storing both v_get_pixel words) and logs "NewTOS contract (ADR-038), no
# oracle". EmuTOS has no path above 16 planes (vdi_defs.h:22): the values
# below are the contract's -- ADR-038 (docs/MEMORY.md) and the 32-plane
# sections of docs/api/vdi/raster/_raster.md (V63 R1-R6, V64 P1-P9, V65
# sections 2-6) -- and tosdump/host/contract32-check.py lays them beside
# every case, computed from the case line itself. Its dump is a regression
# baseline (NEWTOS32-...), never an oracle reference.
# Run: cargo xtask tosdump rast tosdump/cases/vdi-raster-screen32.tsv
#      --out <dir> --bootargs vdiplanes=32
#   opcode <TAB> intin <TAB> ptsin <TAB> src <TAB> dst <TAB> fill <TAB> comment
# Derived line by line from vdi-raster-screen.tsv: every 16-plane memory
# form is a 32-plane one (a 32x16 form is 1024 WORDs, the whole wide
# buffer), and two refusal cases are added (E19, F21). Section E is
# changed by the rule below.
# THE WORDS THIS TABLE EXPECTS (docs/TOS-REFERENCE-DUMPER.md, "The
# expected values at 32"):
#   pen pixel       0x00RRGGBB, each gun q = (c * 255 + 500) / 1000 (V64
#   memory pixel    fd_nplanes 32: native 32-bit 0xXXRRGGBB, row fd_wdwidth
#                   * 16 pixels; on AArch64 pixel k is WORD 2k (low), 2k+1
#                   (high) (V65 section 3)
#   logic ops       bitwise on all 32 bits, X included; ALL_WHITE 0,
#                   ALL_BLACK 0xFFFFFFFF (V63 R4)
#   readback        v_get_pixel: INTOUT[0] = 0x00RR, INTOUT[1] = 0xGGBB, X
#                   masked (V65 section 6); stored high word first at buffer
#                   B[2 * (row * 32 + col)]. A cleared screen reads
#                   {0x00FF, 0xFFFF}, the same as pen 0 (V63 R5)
#   refusals        a memory form of 9..31 planes (16 included) against the
#                   32-plane screen: s_nxwd != d_nxwd, silent no-op (V65
#                   section 2, O5)
# THE X RULE ("paint before you copy"). The byte above R, G, B of a screen
# pixel no pen wrote is implementation-defined (v_clrwk may fill 0xFF or
# 0x00FFFFFF, V63 R3), and a raw Screen -> Memory copy carries it (V65
# section 3). So every case of section E whose result reads a screen pixel
# first paints the source rectangle with a pen (a pen writes X = 0, V63
# R2); the memory result is then exact in all 32 bits. The readbacks of
# sections F, G and H go through v_get_pixel, which masks X. The checker
# refuses a table whose expected memory word depends on an unpainted pixel.
# The reset before every case (runner.c, td_reset_vdi) clears the screen
# with v_clrwk and sets vs_clip off, vsf_interior solid, vsf_color 1.
!screen
# SECTION E -- vro_cpyfm (109) SCREEN -> MEMORY at 32 planes.
# Source S, destination buffer B as a 32x16 form at 32 planes (1024
# WORDs, the whole wide buffer). The screen counts as 32 planes; the copy
# runs on the raw 32-bit store word (V65 section 3). No clipping: the
# destination is not the screen. Every source rectangle is painted first.

column7: E1 pen 1 fill to memory: 512 x 0x00000000
E2 pen 5 at the origin to memory: 512 x 0x0000FFFF

column1: # the op runs on all 32 bits: the painted X (0) meets the fill's high byte
# NOT_D reads no source: nothing to paint
# a vr_recfl pen fill (solid, replace, after the reset) then copied: the
# pen's pixel, X 0

column7: E8 pen 2 fill to memory: 512 x 0x00FF0000
E9 partial pen 3 fill: rows 4-11 cols 8-23 0x0000FF00, rest 0x00FFFFFF

column1: # pen 0 is 0x00FFFFFF: X 0, not the cleared screen's undefined X

column7: E10 pen 0 fill to memory: 512 x 0x00FFFFFF

column1: # a memory destination anchor off the origin: d_xmin/d_ymin and the
# 32-plane row of fd_wdwidth * 16 pixels

column7: E11 16x8 pen 4 block to memory (8,4): 0x000000FF there, fill elsewhere

column1: # two pens whose guns are not 0 or 255: the 8-bit quantisation
# the rules on the screen path

column7: E13 destination 4 planes: s_nxwd != d_nxwd, no-op
E14 PAT_FLAG|3 on the truecolor path: nothing copied
E15 reversed source corners: sorted copy, PTSIN unchanged
E18 XOR a red screen into the fill: B = fill ^ 0x00FF0000

column1: # a 16-plane memory form against the 32-plane screen: refused (O5)

column7: E19 destination 16 planes at 32: refused, B keeps the fill

column1: # SECTION F -- vro_cpyfm (109) MEMORY -> SCREEN, read back.
# Source buffer A (32x16, 32 planes: the fill read as 32-bit pixels),
# destination S, written raw (V65 section 3). Clipping only if vs_clip is
# on (:947-949) -- the reset turns it off, so dont_clip (:882-900). The
# readback window (100,60) 32x16 is the destination rectangle, or a larger
# window so an over-draw at the border would show as a pixel that is not
# the cleared {0x00FF, 0xFFFF}. The readback masks X.

column7: F1 the whole form to the screen: readback = fill(31) & 0x00FFFFFF
F2 16x8 from (8,4) to (101,61): rows 1-8 cols 1-16, cleared border
F3 XOR onto the cleared screen: ~fill, RGB
F4 AND onto the cleared screen: fill, RGB
F5 NOTS_AND_D onto the cleared screen: ~fill, RGB
F9 ALL_BLACK: 0xFFFFFFFF, reads as the cleared screen
F11 PAT_FLAG|3 on the truecolor path: nothing drawn
F12 source 8 planes: s_nxwd != d_nxwd, no-op

column1: # clipping, destination screen (do_clip, :809-877): the visible part
# keeps its source offset -- s_xmin moves with d_xmin (:824-826)

column7: F13 clipped to (104,62)-(127,73): fill inside, cleared outside
vs_clip on, cutting right and bottom
F14 clip ends at (115,67): cols 0-15 rows 0-7 only
F15 reversed destination corners: lands at (100,60) (arb_corner)
F20 source at (5,3), not word aligned: fill[(3+r)*32+5+c]

column1: # a 16-plane memory form against the 32-plane screen: refused (O5)

column7: F21 source 16 planes at 32: refused, the screen stays cleared

column1: # SECTION G -- vro_cpyfm (109) SCREEN -> SCREEN, overlapping.
# A prelude lays a 16x8 block of the fill at the source rectangle; the
# case moves it by (8,4), (8,0) or (0,4) in each direction so that the
# destination overlaps the source.  EmuTOS chooses the copy direction by
# comparing the two START ADDRESSES (vro_cpyfm16, :993; at 32 the same start-address rule, V65 section 3): src < dst ->
# start at s_xmax/s_ymax and d_xmax/d_ymax, step -1 (:994-999).  On one
# screen that is: reverse iff the destination is lower, or on the same
# row and further right.  NewTOS decides rows and columns separately
# (the kernel backend's copy_rect: down = dy > sy, right = dx > sx); for a
# screen the two rules give the same picture -- which this section
# measures rather than argues.  Every pixel of the fill differs, so a
# copy that eats itself is visible.  PTSIN[6..7] is always consistent
# with the source extent (D-VDI-25 / R01 is deferred and not restated).

column7: G1 down and right by (8,4): backwards path
G2 up and left by (8,4): forwards path
G3 right by 8, same rows: backwards, column order decides
G4 left by 8, same rows: forwards
G5 down by 4, same columns: backwards, row order decides
G6 up by 4, same columns: forwards
G7 down and left: backwards rows, EmuTOS also backwards columns
G8 up and right: forwards rows, EmuTOS also forwards columns

column1: # XOR over the overlap: an earlier write is read back as source later
# only if the directions differ, so the picture is the direction

column7: G11 onto itself: src == dst, forwards, unchanged
G12 XOR onto itself: RGB 0 over the block
G14 down and right, clipped to (104,62)-(127,73)
G16 PAT_FLAG|3 screen to screen: nothing copied
G17 to the origin, far apart: the block at (0,0), cleared border

column1: # SECTION H -- vrt_cpyfm (121) MONO -> SCREEN, read back.
# Source buffer A as a 1-plane 32x16 form (two words per row, MSB first,
# the fill's bits), destination S.  The source must be one plane
# (s_nxwd == 2, :1384); fg/bg = validate_color_index(INTIN[1..2]) (ncol
# 256 at 32), drawn as the pens' 32-bit pixels (V64 P3, the screen path
# blit_mono, V65 section 4): MD_REPLACE fg/bg, MD_TRANS fg on set bits,
# MD_XOR the complement on set bits, MD_ERASE bg on clear bits.  The
# readback masks X: the expected pixels are the pens' RGB.

column7: H2 MD_TRANS pen 1: set 0x000000, clear stays cleared
H3 MD_XOR on the cleared screen: set RGB 0
H4 MD_ERASE bg pen 0: clear 0xFFFFFF, set stays cleared
H7 MD_ERASE bg yellow: clear 0xFFFF00, set stays cleared
H8 MD_XOR on red: set RGB 0x00FFFF, clear 0xFF0000
H9 pens out of range: validate_color_index -> 1, all 0x000000
H11 source at (5,3), not word aligned: bits (3+r, 5+c), cleared border

column1: # PREDICTED DIFFERENCE, see the head of the file

column7: H12 PAT_FLAG|MD_REPLACE on the truecolor path: nothing drawn
H13 the screen as a mono source: not one plane, no-op

column1: # a 32-plane MEMORY destination (V65 section 4): the pen pixels, all 32
# bits; MD_XOR complements all 32 bits

column7: H17 MD_REPLACE into memory: set 0x00FF0000, clear 0x000000FF
H18 MD_XOR into memory: set ~fill(124), clear fill(124), 32 bits
